newsitem.title: INDIA: India police, students clash in capital.
newsitem.headline: India police, students clash in capital.

text.p: Several dozen people were injured on Tuesday when police in the Indian capital used batons, teargas and water cannon to break up a demonstration over the killing of a student leader, eyewitnesses said.

About 3,000 members of the All India Students Association (AISA) took part in the protest, which turned violent when demonstrators attempted to march towards Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's office, they said.

The students were protesting against the death of Chandrashekhar (one name), former president of New Delhi's Jawaharlal Nehru University, who was killed on March 31 by supporters of a rival group, organisers said.
AISA leader Mithu Paul said about four dozen students were injured, including at least three seriously, when police dispersed the demonstration.
AISA general secretary Ranjit Abhigyan said students threw stones at police and buildings after they were struck with batons.
Authorities said an unspecified number of police suffered minor injuries.
